newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KLINSMANN THREATENS TO LEAVE BAYERN MUNICH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN THREATENS TO LEAVE BAYERN MUNICH.

text.p: Germany's captain and striker Juergen Klinsmann threatened on Sunday to leave Bayern Munich because he is not happy with the way he is being treated at the club.

Klinsmann has scored just five goals this season, way below the Bundesliga's leading scorers, and is unhappy with the defensive tactics of the German league leaders who are coached by experienced Italian Giovanni Trapattoni.

"If it goes on like this, I'm leaving," Germany's Euro 96 captain said as the Bundesliga began its two-month winter break. "I have had to swallow a lot and I'm prepared to swallow a lot more to win the German championship.
"But when everyone takes it out on me, I have to ask myself whether I belong here."
Last weekend Klinsmann faced the embarrassment of being substituted in the second half of Bayern's top-of-the-table clash at VfB Stuttgart, where he first made his name in Germany.

Bayern have scored far fewer goals than their rivals Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and Stuttgart. Klinsmann has had to play second fiddle to the Bundesliga chief marksman and rising star Sean Dundee of Karlsruhe who has hit 13. South African-born Dundee wants to play for Germany.
Klinsmann, 32, came to Bayern from England's Tottenham Hotspur two seasons ago because he wanted to join a club which would play a regular role in the European competitions.

Although Bayern won the UEFA Cup last season, they went out in the first round of the competition this season and have been criticised for being too defensive this season despite their position at the top.

Klinsmann's contract at Bayern runs until June 30 1998 but his criticism of the club is sure to prompt speculation that the striker may be tempted to return to England where he was a very popular figure.
The striker does have an opt-out clause in his contract which would allow him to leave at the end of the season.
"I have been in Munich one-and-an-half years and always believed things would get better. But nothing has got better," he said.
